Introduction

🧙🏾‍♂️ Absolutely. The reading application should include a proper user registration and login system, with each user having a separate library, reading progress, notes, highlights, and vocabulary.

A good first architecture is:

book_reader/
├── app.py
├── requirements.txt
├── README.md
├── config.py
│
├── data/
│   └── book_reader.db
│
├── models/
│   ├── user.py
│   ├── book.py
│   ├── annotation.py
│   └── vocabulary.py
│
├── routes/
│   ├── auth.py
│   ├── library.py
│   └── reader.py
│
├── templates/
│   ├── base.html
│   ├── index.html
│   ├── login.html
│   ├── register.html
│   ├── library.html
│   ├── reader.html
│   ├── notes.html
│   └── vocabulary.html
│
├── static/
│   ├── css/
│   │   └── styles.css
│   └── js/
│       └── reader.js
│
└── uploads/
    └── books/

The user workflow becomes:

Register
   ↓
Login
   ↓
My Library
   ↓
Import / Open Book
   ↓
Read
   ├── Bookmark
   ├── Highlight
   ├── Add Note
   ├── Save Vocabulary
   └── Track Progress
   ↓
Logout

The database would connect all reading information to a particular user:

users
├── id
├── username
├── email
├── password_hash
└── created_at

books
├── id
├── user_id
├── title
├── author
├── language
├── file_path
└── created_at

reading_progress
├── id
├── user_id
├── book_id
├── position
└── updated_at

annotations
├── id
├── user_id
├── book_id
├── selected_text
├── note
└── created_at

vocabulary
├── id
├── user_id
├── book_id
├── word
├── language
├── definition
└── created_at

For authentication, I recommend Flask-Login + Werkzeug password hashing + SQLite/SQLAlchemy. Passwords would never be stored directly; registration would store only a hashed password, and Flask sessions would keep the user logged in securely.

The first usable version should include these features:

  1. Register account.

  2. Log in and log out.

  3. Protect pages so unauthenticated users cannot access the library.

  4. Give every user a separate personal library.

  5. Upload/import .txt and .md books.

  6. Read books in the browser.

  7. Save reading position.

  8. Add bookmarks and notes.

  9. Save vocabulary while reading.

  10. Search the user's own books and vocabulary.

The login page could be:

┌────────────────────────────────────┐
│             Book Reader            │
│                                    │
│ Email / Username                   │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │                                │ │
│ └────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                    │
│ Password                           │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ ••••••••                       │ │
│ └────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                    │
│          [ Log In ]                │
│                                    │
│ New user? Create an account        │
└────────────────────────────────────┘

And after login:

Book Reader                         Ruixing ▼
─────────────────────────────────────────────
My Library   Vocabulary   Notes   Logout

Search books...                     + Add Book

The Civil War in the United States
██████████████░░░░  72%
Continue Reading

Capital
██████░░░░░░░░░░░░  31%
Continue Reading

聊斋志异
█████████░░░░░░░░░  48%
Continue Reading

I suggest we implement Version 1 with Flask + SQLite + Flask-Login + TXT/Markdown reading first, then add PDF and EPUB after the authentication/library foundation is stable.

🧙🏾‍♂️ Recommended next step: I can now generate the complete Version 1 project scaffold and working registration/login system, including app.py, database models, routes, HTML pages, CSS, requirements.txt, and startup instructions.
